hero.teaser_short_description: Thymosin Alpha-1 is a 28-amino-acid synthetic peptide corresponding to the thymic peptide Tα1, known pharmaceutically as thymalfasin. Veracue supplies it as a research material for laboratory work. The most rigorous published evidence (the TESTS phase 3 trial, BMJ 2025) tested Tα1 against placebo in 1,106 adults with sepsis — a randomized, controlled clinical trial — and found no clear reduction in 28-day mortality. Earlier trials and pooled analyses have reported mixed results, so this material does not establish a treatment effect or immune benefit in people.

product_details.overview:
Thymosin Alpha-1 (Tα1) is a 28-amino-acid acidic peptide, Nα-acetylated at the serine terminus, originally isolated from calf thymus extract ("thymosin fraction 5") in 1977 and later shown to be a proteolytic fragment of the precursor protein prothymosin alpha. The synthetic version is known by the international non-proprietary name thymalfasin, marketed outside the United States under the brand name Zadaxin. Veracue supplies Thymosin Alpha-1 as a research material for laboratory immunology work — not as thymalfasin, Zadaxin, or any pharmaceutical product.

Tα1 is one of the more clinically studied synthetic peptides in the research-peptide space: it has regulatory approval or registration in roughly three dozen countries (primarily for chronic hepatitis B and as a vaccine/immune adjuvant) and U.S. FDA orphan-drug designations for several indications, but it does not hold full FDA approval and is not sold in the United States as a drug. That regulatory history outside the U.S. is a fact about the molecule's development, not a claim about this research product, which is labeled Research Use Only and is not for human or veterinary administration.
product_details.intended_use:
This material is offered for in vitro and laboratory research — for example, immune-cell signaling studies, toll-like-receptor (TLR) pathway work, dendritic-cell maturation assays, T-cell differentiation research, or analytical method development. It is not a drug, supplement, or food, and it is not intended for administration to humans or animals.

Research-use positioning is not only a label. Nothing on this page provides, or should be read as, dosing, reconstitution-for-administration, or treatment information.

molecular_identity.narrative: Thymosin Alpha-1 is the first 28 residues of prothymosin alpha, with the N-terminal serine acetylated. Unlike many research peptides where suppliers report several competing molecular-weight values for different salt or complex forms, Tα1's identity is well standardized in the literature: essentially every source (PubChem, ChemicalBook, peptide-synthesis vendors, and the primary isolation literature) converges on the same sequence, formula, and mass.
molecular_identity.note: These are reference-chemistry values for the Thymosin Alpha-1 molecule as documented across chemical databases and the synthesis literature — not a Veracue-specific analytical result. Veracue's own lot-specific purity, net peptide content, and any Certificate of Analysis must come from first-party testing once a batch is produced and listed.

what_the_research_shows.intro: Tα1 has a genuinely large clinical literature compared with most research peptides in this catalog — this section separates what different tiers of that evidence actually show, because a molecule with decades of study still has areas of real uncertainty, and evidence for the molecule is not the same as evidence for this specific research material.
what_the_research_shows.mechanism_summary: Preclinical and mechanistic studies describe Tα1 acting through Toll-like receptor signaling — primarily TLR9 (via the MyD88-dependent pathway, contributing to type I interferon production) and TLR2 (via MyD88- and TRIF-dependent pathways) on dendritic cells and other innate immune cells. Downstream of this, laboratory studies report dendritic-cell maturation (increased CD80/CD86 and MHC class I/II expression), modulation of Th1-associated cytokines such as IL-2 and IFN-γ, and effects on T-cell differentiation and NK-cell activity. Some studies also describe a regulatory/tolerogenic arm — TLR9-dependent induction of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) leading to regulatory T-cell generation — indicating the peptide's immune effects are better described as modulatory than simply stimulatory.

clinical_evidence_by_indication.evidence_type: Multiple randomized controlled trials plus a 2025 phase 3 trial and meta-analyses
clinical_evidence_by_indication.summary: Earlier, smaller randomized trials (e.g., the ETASS trial, 2013) and several meta-analyses have reported reduced 28-day mortality with Tα1 as an adjunct in severe sepsis. However, the largest and most recent trial — TESTS, a multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 1,106 adults (BMJ, 2025; corrected 2025) — found no clear evidence that Tα1 reduces 28-day all-cause mortality (23.4% Tα1 vs 24.1% placebo; hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77–1.27). A 2025 updated systematic review and trial-sequential meta-analysis pooling 11 RCTs reported a statistically significant reduction in 28-day mortality (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.59–0.90) but explicitly flagged that the required information size had not been reached and that heterogeneity across trials was high, with a prespecified subgroup analysis in TESTS itself suggesting the effect (if any) may differ by age and diabetes status.
clinical_evidence_by_indication.current_read: The evidence is genuinely mixed. Older, smaller trials and some pooled analyses lean positive; the largest, most rigorous single trial to date does not confirm a mortality benefit. This should not be presented as either 'proven to help' or 'proven not to work' — both a positive and a negative claim currently go beyond what the totality of evidence supports.

clinical_evidence_by_indication.evidence_type: Multiple clinical trials outside the U.S.; basis for regulatory approvals in other countries
clinical_evidence_by_indication.summary: Tα1 (as thymalfasin) has been studied as an antiviral adjunct in chronic hepatitis B and C, including in combination with interferon, and this indication underlies its approval/registration in roughly three dozen countries outside the United States.
clinical_evidence_by_indication.current_read: This body of evidence concerns a pharmaceutical product (thymalfasin) administered under medical supervision in specific patient populations — it says nothing about the safety, purity, or handling of a research-grade RUO material sourced from a different manufacturer.

clinical_evidence_by_indication.evidence_type: In vitro dendritic-cell studies and some clinical vaccine-response data
clinical_evidence_by_indication.summary: In vitro work shows Tα1 modulates human dendritic-cell responses to viral and bacterial TLR agonists (enhancing HLA-I/II expression and IL-6/TNF-α/IL-8 secretion in some contexts), and it has been investigated clinically as a vaccine-response enhancer.
clinical_evidence_by_indication.current_read: This is a research-supported mechanism with some human data, but findings vary by stimulus, cell type, and study design — it is not a general claim that the peptide boosts immunity in every context.

clinical_evidence_by_indication.evidence_type: Preclinical and some clinical investigation, including in combination with checkpoint inhibitors in patent literature
clinical_evidence_by_indication.summary: Tα1 has been studied for its potential to reduce hematologic toxicity of cytotoxic chemotherapy and as a potential combination agent with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
clinical_evidence_by_indication.current_read: This remains an active but not definitively established research area; it is not evidence of anticancer efficacy for this research material.

what_this_research_does_not_show: That Thymosin Alpha-1 is proven to reduce mortality in sepsis — the largest phase 3 trial to date did not confirm this
That findings from thymalfasin/Zadaxin (a regulated pharmaceutical product used under medical supervision) apply to this or any other RUO research material
That the molecule's TLR/dendritic-cell mechanism translates into a general claim of 'boosting the immune system' in any uncontrolled setting
That Veracue's specific research material has been independently tested — that data does not yet exist and will be published once available

quality_and_purity.reading_a_coa: A purity percentage on its own answers only one question. A useful Thymosin Alpha-1 Certificate of Analysis (COA) should let you confirm what the material is, how pure it is by a stated method, how much is actually in the vial, and that the report belongs to the lot you received. Because Tα1 is a 28-residue peptide, mass-spectrometry identity confirmation and net peptide content are particularly informative alongside HPLC purity, since single amino-acid deletions or truncations are the most common synthesis impurity in a peptide this length.

faq.a: Thymosin Alpha-1 (Tα1) is a 28-amino-acid, Nα-acetylated peptide fragment of the precursor protein prothymosin alpha, studied in immunology research. Veracue supplies it as a laboratory research material only.

faq.q: Is Thymosin Alpha-1 the same as thymalfasin or Zadaxin?
faq.a: Thymalfasin is the international non-proprietary name for synthetic Thymosin Alpha-1, marketed outside the U.S. under the brand name Zadaxin as a regulated pharmaceutical. Veracue's product is a separate research-grade material and is not sold, labeled, or intended as that pharmaceutical product.

faq.q: What is the amino acid sequence and molecular weight of Thymosin Alpha-1?
faq.a: The sequence is Ac-Ser-Asp-Ala-Ala-Val-Asp-Thr-Ser-Ser-Glu-Ile-Thr-Thr-Lys-Asp-Leu-Lys-Glu-Lys-Lys-Glu-Val-Val-Glu-Glu-Ala-Glu-Asn-OH (molecular formula C129H215N33O55), with an average molecular weight of 3108.3 g/mol and a monoisotopic mass of 3106.50 Da (CAS 62304-98-7).

faq.q: What does Thymosin Alpha-1 research focus on?
faq.a: Research on Tα1 centers on its interaction with Toll-like receptors TLR2 and TLR9 on dendritic cells, its effects on dendritic-cell maturation and antigen presentation, T-cell differentiation, NK-cell activity, and modulation of cytokine networks such as IL-2, IFN-γ, and IFN-α.

faq.q: Does thymosin alpha-1 research show a benefit in sepsis?
faq.a: The evidence is mixed. Some earlier randomized trials and pooled meta-analyses report a reduction in 28-day sepsis mortality, but the largest and most recent phase 3 trial (TESTS, BMJ 2025, n=1,106) found no clear evidence of a mortality benefit. Neither a clear positive nor a clear negative conclusion is currently supported.

faq.q: What was the 2025 BMJ TESTS trial?
faq.a: TESTS was a multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial across 22 centres in China (1,106 adults with sepsis) that compared subcutaneous Tα1 with placebo. 28-day all-cause mortality was 23.4% in the Tα1 group versus 24.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77–1.27) — the trial concluded there was no clear evidence that Tα1 decreases 28-day mortality in adults with sepsis.

faq.q: Has Thymosin Alpha-1 been studied in humans?
faq.a: Yes. As thymalfasin, it has been studied in thousands of patients across clinical trials for chronic hepatitis B and C, sepsis, and as a vaccine adjuvant, and is approved or registered in roughly three dozen countries outside the United States — though it does not hold full FDA approval and is not sold as a drug in the U.S.

No. It is not FDA-approved as a drug in the United States, though it has received FDA orphan-drug designation for several indications and full marketing approval in other countries. Veracue's material is supplied strictly as a Research Use Only laboratory compound.

faq.q: What is the difference between Thymosin Alpha-1 and Thymosin Beta-4 / TB-500?
faq.a: They are unrelated peptides from the same historical thymus-extract fraction family. Thymosin Alpha-1 is a 28-residue immune-signaling peptide acting through TLR pathways. Thymosin Beta-4 is a distinct, larger actin-binding peptide involved in cell migration and tissue repair, and TB-500 is a synthetic fragment used as its research analog.

faq.q: What should a Thymosin Alpha-1 Certificate of Analysis include?
faq.a: A useful COA states the lot number, the HPLC purity method and result, mass-spectrometry identity confirmation against the expected ~3108 Da mass, net peptide content, and the testing laboratory and date.

faq.q: What does Research Use Only mean for this product?
faq.a: Research Use Only means the compound is intended strictly for laboratory and scientific research — not for human or veterinary consumption, diagnosis, or treatment. It has not been evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy in those other contexts.
